title: Auth Control Plane OpenID discovery metadata (v1 wire format)
description:
The document served at GET /.well-known/openid-configuration (TRD section 15): a deliberately small SUBSET of OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 section 3 metadata. It exists so a resource service can find the issuer's JWKS (jwks.v1) from one configured issuer URL. The Auth Control Plane is not an OpenID Provider and publishes no authorization, token or userinfo endpoint here, so none is declared; `additionalProperties: false` makes adding one a v2 decision rather than an accident.

WHAT A SCHEMA CAN SAY. `issuer` and `jwks_uri` are https URLs with a fixed shape (no userinfo, query or fragment, lowercase ASCII host, no trailing slash on the issuer), written with explicit character ranges so Go RE2, Python and ECMA-262 agree. `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` is exactly ["EdDSA"] (TRD section 11): no symmetric algorithm and no `none` can be advertised.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY, AND THE CLIENT RULES THAT CLOSE IT. JSON Schema cannot compare two members of one instance, nor an instance against configuration. Three rules are therefore client rules (internal/auth/contracts ParseDiscovery, authclient.discovery.parse_discovery), pinned by the manifest's `reject_by_client` fixtures, which are valid against this schema on purpose:
  1. `jwks_uri` must equal `issuer` + `/.well-known/jwks.json`, and `issuer` must equal the URL prefix the document was fetched from (OpenID Connect Discovery section 4.3).
  2. ISSUER PINNING. The client pins the expected issuer per credential class in its configuration and rejects a discovery document from any other issuer, however well-formed. Platform access/workload-token keys and ACR Web-assertion keys are separate issuers (TRD section 12); keeping them apart is this pin.
  3. Token-class confusion is settled by the token's own `typ`, `aud` and `iss` claims (TRD section 11), never by discovery metadata.

Plain http is not part of this wire format. A loopback or Compose deployment that serves http is a local-development configuration (TRD section 6) and does not publish a conforming v1 document.

issuer.description: The issuer identifier: an https origin with an optional path prefix. No trailing slash, query, fragment or userinfo (OpenID Connect Discovery section 3). It equals the `iss` of every token this issuer signs.

jwks_uri.description: Where the issuer's jwks.v1 document is served. Must equal `issuer` + `/.well-known/jwks.json`; the schema pins only the shape, the equality is a client rule (see the schema description).

id_token_signing_alg_values_supported.description: Exactly EdDSA, TRD section 11. A const rather than an enum-in-items so that an added algorithm, `none` and symmetric algorithms included, fails as a whole.
